The main takeaway from our work is that

the compartmentalized metabolic scheme for glutamic acid, as originally proposed by Kaczmarek and co-workers, is a useful tool for the interpretation of the results of amino acid determinations in nervous tissue.

the glial compartment of the nervous tissue is not a static, unalterable structure but can be affected by a variety of different conditions, which may be associated with altered neuronal functions or structural changes.
a compartmentalized metabolic scheme for glutamic acid is not only valid but can be used to study the effects of altered cerebral conditions on the metabolic pathways of glutamic acid.
